# Valve cover gasket replacement

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Disconnect wires and remove components above the driver side intake plenum before replacing valve cover gaskets. [t1549]

Remove the upper intake manifold gasket first, then cut two back engine coolant lines to avoid removing clamps. [t1061]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Disconnect all basic electrical wires visible over the valve covers.
2. Remove or unhook components sitting on top of the driver side intake plenum to access it from above.
3. [Partial] Address two coolant hoses located at the back of the plenum by either cutting and replacing them, swapping out old ones for new bungee cords with clips, or removing one entirely.

_Procedure reported by [t1549]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1061] [Partial]</summary>

1. Remove the upper intake manifold gasket first.
2. Cut two coolant lines located at the back of the engine to avoid removing clamps.

</details>

## Tools

- Various length screwdrivers (short/stub, medium, long) [t1549]
- Bungee cord [t1549]

- [Partial] Coolant hoses or bungee cords [t1549]

## Tips & gotchas

- Document each removal step by taking pictures and writing notes. [t1549]
- Use a short bungee cord to hang the plenum from the hood if you want to leave coolant hoses connected in the back. [t1549]
- Cutting coolant lines is easier than removing clamps. [t1061]
- [Partial] Using an upper intake gasket prevents future removal issues. [t1061]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Forcing old, brittle lower coolant hoses without cutting them first, [t1549]
